etymologies.etymologyHTML: From Middle English undernethe, undernethen, from Old English underneoþan (“underneath”), ultimately from Proto-Germanic *underniþer.

quote.citation: 1825, Isaac Taylor, Scenes of British Wealth: In Produce, Manufactures, and Commerce, for the Amusement and Instruction of Little Tarry At-home Travellers‎[1]:
quote.text: connected with it underneath, you see a very fine hair-spring.

definitions.definition: On the underside or lower face.

quote.citation: 1832, Georges Cuvier, translated by Edward Griffith, edited by Georges Cuvier, Edward Pidgeon, and Edward Griffith, The Animal Kingdom: Arranged in Conformity with Its Organization‎[2], volume 14, published 2012, →ISBN:
quote.text: No insects exhibit, like them, what may be termed four net-work eyes. It is very easy to perceive them in looking at the animal from above, and then examining it underneath

definitions.definition: Under the control or power of.

quote.text: The mess in the kitchen was one thing. The way the place smelled was another—some sort of chemistry-lab stink on top, some other smell underneath it. He was afraid the underneath smell might be blood.

quote.citation: 1938, Xavier Herbert, chapter V, in Capricornia‎[3], page 64:
quote.text: Nawnim yelped, heaved away, struck his head on the underneath of the bed, and rolled into view bawling.

quote.citation: 2002, Mary Ann Caws, Surrealist Painters and Poets: An Anthology‎[4], page 229:
quote.text: It was a monolith of a golden color, opening at its base on to a cavern: its underneath was hollowed out by water.

quote.citation: 2010, Molly Brodak, A Little Middle of the Night‎[5], page 13:
quote.text: I have been looking for an underneath I couldn't see.

quote.citation: 2011, Nigella Lawson, Nigella Express: Good Food Fast‎[6]:
quote.text: they harden up a little as they cool, and they should be damp within; that's what makes them chewy, so don't worry that the underneaths of the macaroons look sticky.

definitions.definition: A background radio sound track played during a specific announcement or program.

quote.citation: 2009, Jay Trachtenberg (radio host), KUT-FM Radio, Austin, Texas, 17 Dec.:
quote.text: The underneath is music from the latest album by [...].
